{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABeoj6Mw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhIJx_k", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 347, "title": "Share one Chrome tab audio capture across multiple concurrent Live graph windows", "body": "## Goal

Support **two or more independent Live graph execution windows processing audio from the *same Chrome tab at the same time***.

Today, Graph A can start capturing a tab, but Graph B targeting the same tab fails with an error such as **“Cannot capture a tab with an active stream. Start a new session to retry.”** Chrome does not permit a second independent tab capture for that target. The extension should **capture the tab only once and fan out its PCM stream to every authorized active graph session targeting that tab**.

Example: one tab playing a meeting/video → Graph A performs transcription while Graph B independently runs translation or a different speech pipeline. Both must receive the same captured audio without a second `chrome.tabCapture` request.

## Current implementation / cause

- [`extension/tab-source.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/tab-source.js): each `ExtensionTab` independently calls `chrome.tabCapture.getMediaStreamId({targetTabId: this.tabId})`, then `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia(...chromeMediaSource:'tab'...)` and establishes audio processing. It also restores the captured tab's speaker playback.
- [`extension/tab-audio-node.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/tab-audio-node.js): `ExtensionTabAudioNode` creates its own `ExtensionTab` via `sourceFactory`.
- [`extension/graph-runtime.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph-runtime.js) creates a `ChromeTabAudio` source for each Live graph runtime. Separate Live windows currently own independent session/runtime/worker lifecycles, so their separate tab-capture requests conflict even though the graph sessions themselves can coexist.
- [`extension/manifest.json`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/manifest.json) already declares `tabCapture` and `offscreen` permissions.
- [#259](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/issues/259) explicitly allows independent simultaneous Live/Web sessions rather than a global inference lock. Keep that independence: **share the read-only tab audio source, not inference models, graph instances or session state**.

## Required behavior

### One shared capture per target tab, many independent consumers

1. Introduce an extension-owned, **tab-ID-keyed capture coordinator**: for the same tab, concurrent acquisition/subscription requests must coalesce into **exactly one actual `chrome.tabCapture` media capture** (including simultaneous first-start races).
2. Normalize/capture the audio once using the existing supported PCM contract (mono 16 kHz), then fan out ordered audio frames to **all subscribed Live `ChromeTabAudio` Node consumers** without allowing one consumer to alter another's buffers. Preserve semantics of frame ordering, timestamp/flush/stop where relevant, and avoid duplicate/omitted frames during subscription/startup.
3. Each Live window retains its **own selected graph ID/snapshot, runtime, ASR/translation workers, model state, output destinations, Start/Stop/Cancel, error handling, and displays**. Do not add a global model-inference lock or unintended shared mutable processing state.
4. Preserve **user intent and permissions**: a window opening/going Ready must not silently start audio capture. Start creates/joins capture only for the specific originally targeted tab, under the existing toolbar-invocation authorization/permission flow. A second window must not attach to audio from a different tab or become authorized by an unrelated browser tab.
5. Windows targeting **different tabs** must have separate captures and independent lifecycle. Graphs with no `ChromeTabAudio` continue to work as before.
6. Existing multiple `ChromeTabAudio` Nodes **within one graph** must continue sharing/receiving the correct tab audio without extra capture or duplicated playback.

### Correct lifecycle and sound output

7. **Stopping/closing/canceling Graph A removes only A's subscriptions**; if Graph B still consumes the same tab, the underlying capture stays alive and B continues receiving audio. Stopping the *last* consumer releases `MediaStream` tracks, AudioContext/worklet, listeners, and other resources promptly.
8. Handle captured-tab navigation/close, media stream `ended`, permission errors, rapid Stop→Start, window crash/reload, browser suspension/restart, and simultaneous unsubscribe/reacquire without zombie captures, leaked subscriptions, stale handlers, or wrong-tab reassignment. Unexpected capture termination should notify each affected subscriber with an actionable error/ended event; unrelated tabs and sessions stay intact.
9. **Restore captured tab audio to the user's speakers exactly once per captured tab**, not once per subscriber. No doubled playback, echoes, feedback, muted playback after last detach, or changes to independent microphone capture.
10. A late subscriber should receive **live audio from its actual subscription point onward** (no unexpected replay of prior captured speech). Keep frame distribution bounded and nonblocking, with independently controlled queues/backpressure so a slow/failed graph doesn't stall other consumers or accumulate unbounded PCM.
11. Use a robust Chrome MV3 architecture suitable for cross-window ownership (e.g. a per-extension offscreen document owning capture plus message-port subscriptions, or another tested equivalent). **Do not rely on a service worker remaining alive indefinitely or a mutable in-memory singleton inside one Live window**. If introducing an offscreen document, coordinate creation races, lifetime, and authorized tab capture; avoid changing manifest/permissions unnecessarily.
12. Clearly distinguish actual browser/device tab-capture errors from the eliminated duplicate-capture scenario. No silent fallback to another tab, microphone, or a different graph.

## Acceptance criteria / tests

- [ ] Two Live windows launched for the **same tab**, configured with different graphs containing `ChromeTabAudio`, both Start successfully and independently receive nonempty PCM-derived outputs; **only one underlying tab-capture stream** is acquired for that tab.
- [ ] Opening the second Live window during the first one's capture, or starting both nearly simultaneously, does not report “Cannot capture a tab with an active stream”.
- [ ] Each window uses its own graph and model workers; output/graph/session state never crosses between windows.
- [ ] Stop/Cancel/close either Live first; the other continues working. Last subscriber's release stops capture once. Restart/join again works and has no stale frames.
- [ ] Two *different* source tabs can be captured independently and concurrently, with no PCM leak/mix between them.
- [ ] Original tab audio remains audible exactly once; no duplicate audio playback or permanent muting on teardown.
- [ ] Tab close/navigation/stream end, permission denial, canceled initial acquisition, startup races, closing before media grant, and retry produce correct cleanup and session-scoped errors.
- [ ] No audio capture starts merely by opening a Live window or preparing models; source authorization/security behavior is preserved.
- [ ] Normal model-free, microphone-only and Web voice graphs remain unaffected.
- [ ] Add deterministic coordinator/fan-out/lifecycle/concurrency tests plus Chrome MV3 browser integration smoke tests for same-tab dual-graph capture, playback and teardown; document any real-browser limitations honestly.

## Implementation pointers

- `extension/tab-source.js`, `extension/tab-audio-node.js`: replace independent same-tab capture with coordinated capture subscriptions; keep node audio-port contract.
- `extension/graph-runtime.js`, `extension/session.js`, `extension/recorder.js`, `extension/background.js`: wire targeted tab/session identity and clean subscription lifecycle as necessary.
- If using MV3 offscreen capture: add focused coordinator/offscreen modules and lifecycle under `extension/`, preserve extension security policy and verify tab ID/stream authorization.
- Existing `web/audio.js` / `web/capture-worklet.js`: preserve PCM conversion and single audio-playback restoration.
- Tests under `tests/` and documentation explaining concurrent Live tab capture.

## Non-goals

- **Do not implement cross-window inference-model memory sharing** (separate possible future issue).
- Do not impose a single-global-Live-window restriction, serialize unrelated sessions, or automatically terminate the first graph to launch the second.
- Do not redesign Graph Library/toolbars, change model downloads, or change saved graph formats for this feature.

This issue extends the independent-session behavior of #259 with **one-to-many reuse of the tab's captured audio**.
